tldr: The Fed's hawkish 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% now looks absorbed, not feared: S&P and Nasdaq both closed at records Friday (+0.17%, +0.39%) on a second straight up day, with VIX falling a fifth straight session to 14.81 -- though breadth stayed weak underneath (McClellan -34, only ~31-43% of stocks above key MAs), so it's a narrow rally, not broad conviction.

Silver and gold miners extended their post-FOMC rally for a second straight session (SLV +1.63% to $59.93, GLD +0.71% to $401.17) even as oil reversed sharply (WTI -6.3%, Brent -5.8%) -- the levered silver sleeve (1,777oz, 1.589x leverage, NAV S$10.38M) sits 47% from its margin call but still FAILS the 2-week stress-survivability test, so this remains a real, not free, position.

The Trump-Xi summit is now firmly dated Sept 23-25 (leaders meet Sept 24), only 4-6 trading days out -- the next concrete catalyst for FXI/EEM, HK tech and the rare-earth basket (MP, Lynas, JL MAG).
